taxonomy.topic: Chronic kidney disease-mineral and bone disorder
taxonomy.subtopic: Phosphate retention, calcitriol deficiency, and secondary hyperparathyroidism

questions.stem_html: A 58-year-old woman with stage 4 chronic kidney disease has bone pain. Laboratory studies show increased serum phosphate, low-normal calcium, increased parathyroid hormone, and decreased 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D. The accompanying feedback diagram summarizes the altered pathways. Which sequence best explains the increased parathyroid hormone concentration?

options.text_html: Reduced phosphate excretion and reduced renal 1α-hydroxylation lower ionized calcium, stimulating secondary hyperparathyroidism
Increased phosphate excretion raises ionized calcium, directly stimulating parathyroid hormone secretion
Increased calcitriol synthesis decreases intestinal calcium absorption, stimulating parathyroid hyperplasia
Reduced fibroblast growth factor 23 secretion increases urinary phosphate loss and suppresses parathyroid hormone
Primary autonomous parathyroid secretion causes the initial decline in glomerular filtration rate

questions.explanation_html: Loss of functioning nephron mass reduces phosphate excretion and renal 1α-hydroxylase activity. Phosphate retention and reduced calcitriol lower ionized calcium and diminish negative feedback on the parathyroid glands. The resulting secondary hyperparathyroidism increases bone turnover; fibroblast growth factor 23 also rises as an adaptive phosphaturic signal but becomes insufficient as kidney function declines.

wrong_choice_explanations.2: Advanced CKD causes phosphate retention, not increased phosphate excretion, and a rise in ionized calcium would suppress PTH.
wrong_choice_explanations.3: Calcitriol synthesis decreases in CKD; calcitriol normally increases intestinal calcium absorption.
wrong_choice_explanations.4: FGF23 generally increases early in CKD and promotes phosphaturia while suppressing calcitriol synthesis.
wrong_choice_explanations.5: The laboratory pattern is secondary hyperparathyroidism caused by CKD, not primary autonomous parathyroid disease initiating renal failure.

questions.educational_objective: CKD causes phosphate retention and reduced calcitriol production, leading to hypocalcemic signaling and secondary hyperparathyroidism.

media.alt_text: Feedback diagram showing reduced GFR causing phosphate retention and reduced calcitriol, followed by lower calcium signaling and increased parathyroid hormone.
